original_question: For open chaotic scattering systems with hyperbolic trapped sets, does there exist a resonance-free strip of depth gamma > 0 below the real axis at high frequency, and what is the optimal value of that gap? In particular, for obstacle scattering, can the asymptotic resonance gap be as large as gamma_cl / 2, or must it be strictly smaller?
target_in_paper: Section 8.2, 'Is the pressure bound optimal?', especially the explicit obstacle-scattering question on p. 33: 'How large could the resonance gap be for such obstacle problems? Could it be as large as γ_cl/2 ... ?' This is the nearest official formulation of your draft, and it should be read together with Theorem 1, Theorem 3, and Theorem 9, which give the proved pressure-gap criterion that the section is questioning. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's main spectral issue: high-frequency resonance-free strips for chaotic scattering with hyperbolic trapped sets, the relevance of obstacle scattering as the model example, and the specific candidate value γ_cl/2 as the potentially optimal gap beyond the proved pressure bound. It also correctly focuses on the asymptotic/high-frequency regime rather than finite-frequency statements. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's actual open problem is narrower than your first sentence: the existence of a resonance-free strip is already proved under the pressure condition P(-ϕ+/2) < 0 in Theorem 1 for obstacle scattering and Theorem 3 for semiclassical Hamiltonians. The unresolved issue is the optimal size of the gap, not mere existence in full generality. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))

The obstacle model must be specified exactly: the exterior Dirichlet Laplacian for finitely many strictly convex obstacles in ℝ^d satisfying the no-eclipse condition, with trapped set K ⊂ S*Ω for the billiard flow. Your phrase 'open chaotic scattering systems with hyperbolic trapped sets' is broader than the paper's explicit obstacle question. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))

The dynamical quantities need to be defined: ϕ+ is the logarithm of the unstable Jacobian, P(·) is the topological pressure, and γ_cl is not a free parameter but the classical decay rate γ_cl := -P(-ϕ+) > 0. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))

The precise proved gap should be stated: for obstacle scattering, if P(-ϕ+/2) < 0, then for every ε > 0 there exists k_ε > 0 such that there are no resonances in [k_ε, ∞) - i[0, |P(-ϕ+/2)| - ε]. Your draft does not distinguish this established pressure gap from the conjectural larger gap γ_cl/2. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))

The exact high-frequency variable should be fixed. In the obstacle problem the resonances are written in the wavevector variable k, whereas in the semiclassical setting of Theorem 3 the strip is written near a fixed energy E with h → 0. Your draft mixes these settings. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))

To make 'optimal gap' stand-alone, one should define it by a quantifier such as: the supremum Γ such that for every ε > 0 there exists k_ε with no resonances in [k_ε, ∞) - i[0, Γ - ε]. The paper gives an analogous formal definition only for convex co-compact hyperbolic surfaces via the essential spectral gap G(X). ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))

The candidate value γ_cl/2 comes from the random-phase heuristic bound (62), and in the surface case the paper notes that the Jakobson-Naud conjecture G(X) = δ/2 is equivalent to this value. That motivation should be mentioned if γ_cl/2 is singled out. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))

The paper also records an important caveat from numerics: in 3-disk scattering the resonance density has a peak centered near Im k = -γ_cl/2, and if that peak keeps positive width as k → ∞ then the actual gap would be strictly smaller than γ_cl/2. Your draft alludes to the dichotomy but not to this precise mechanism. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))

If you want the question to stay maximally paper-faithful, it should be asked for obstacle scattering; the extension to semiclassical Schrödinger operators is only described as 'very likely' rather than posed as the main formal question. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^d be the exterior of finitely many strictly convex obstacles satisfying the no-eclipse condition, and let Reson(Δ_Ω) be the resonance set of the exterior Dirichlet Laplacian. Assume the billiard flow on the trapped set K ⊂ S*Ω is hyperbolic, let ϕ+ be the logarithm of its unstable Jacobian, and let γ_cl := -P(-ϕ+, Φ^t|_K) > 0 be the classical decay rate. Define the asymptotic obstacle-scattering resonance gap Γ_obs to be the supremum of all Γ ≥ 0 such that, for every ε > 0, there exists k_ε > 0 with Reson(Δ_Ω) ∩ ([k_ε, ∞) - i[0, Γ - ε]) = ∅. Theorem 1 gives Γ_obs ≥ max(0, -P(-ϕ+/2, Φ^t|_K)). Is the true high-frequency gap for such obstacle problems equal to γ_cl/2, i.e. the random-phase candidate suggested by equation (62), or must one have Γ_obs < γ_cl/2? ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))
justification: The review does not state a numbered 'conjecture' for obstacle scattering in the introduction. The nearest paper-faithful target is the explicit open question in §8.2 after equation (65), where Nonnenmacher asks how large the resonance gap can be for convex obstacle problems and whether it could reach γ_cl/2. Theorems 1 and 3 already settle the existence of a pressure-controlled strip, and Theorem 9 plus equation (52) explain how that pressure bound arises from monodromy/open-map dynamics. Section 8.2 then asks whether one can improve beyond P(-ϕ+/2), using the random-phase heuristic (62) and the analogous Jakobson-Naud surface conjecture G(X) = δ/2. That is exactly the paper's intent that your draft is aiming at, but your draft needs the operator, flow, pressure, γ_cl, and quantifier structure made explicit. ([imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~stephane.nonnenmacher/publis/Nonnen2011%28Nonlinearity%29.pdf))
